title: XGS-PON: shared fibre envelopes
simple: A fibre can be shared by many homes. Going home, every house hears the envelopes, but your router keeps only the one with your house number. Going out, homes take turns.
technical: This is an XGS-PON XGEM frame on a PON: about 10 Gbit/s each way (9.953), shared by the homes on the splitter. Downstream is broadcast with per-XGEM-port AES; upstream, each ONT sends a short burst in its own slot inside every 125 µs frame, as the OLT's BWmap assigns after ranging.
extra: The older GPON can share this fibre and splitter: it uses other colours (1490 nm down, 1310 nm up, next to XGS-PON's 1577 and 1270 nm), so each ONT filters out the light it doesn't speak. It runs 2.5 Gbit/s down and 1.25 up with the same idea, but its GEM header is 5 bytes with a 12-bit Port-ID, where XGEM's is 8 bytes with 16.

nat.title: Your router keeps its house number
nat.simple: Your router hears the shared fibre, but it only keeps the light envelope marked House no. 1127. The others stay locked. Underneath, the envelope travels as flashes of light in a glass thread.
nat.technical: At the ONT/router, downstream XGEM frames for all ONTs arrive from the splitter. This ONT accepts XGEM Port-ID 1127, discards other Port-IDs, and relies on per-port AES for privacy.

describe.simple: The road points at your router. One card shows the fibre terminal, a splitter and four houses. Light envelopes go to every house, but only the one marked 1127 opens at your router. The neighbours stay locked. Another card shows the turn strip with slot 3 lit.
describe.technical: The ONT and router view highlights downstream XGEM Port-ID 1127 in the header. Broadcast envelopes fan out through the splitter. Other XGEM frames stay locked, and the accepted one gets a check. The upstream card shows the slots of one 125 microsecond frame with turn 0x467 marked.

bridge.title: The fibre terminal hands out turns
bridge.simple: The fibre terminal is the boss of the shared fibre. It sends a little timetable so each house knows when to talk and nobody talks over anyone else.
bridge.technical: At the OLT, the downstream frame carries a BWmap. Upstream bursts use Alloc-IDs/T-CONTs, DBA grants, and ranging equalisation delays so near and far ONTs land in their assigned slots of each 125 µs frame.

describe.simple: This scene is at the fibre terminal, with cards for the shared fibre. One card sends envelopes through the splitter in the street to four houses. The turn card is active. Its timetable is split into four slots, slot 3 glows, and small bursts drop into their turns one by one.
describe.technical: The OLT view makes the upstream scheduler card active. Four slots share a 125 microsecond frame, with Alloc-ID 0x467 highlighted. Dots and bursts step through the grants. The downstream card still shows splitter broadcast and XGEM Port-ID 1127.
